## Goal

Keep current truth durable while compacting historical precision predictably, recording coverage loss, and separating temporary exports from user-owned evidence bundles.

## Deliverables

- Bounded retention policy
- Snapshot and anomaly compaction
- Retention and coverage records
- Export record and inventory lifecycle
- Boundary and pressure test suite

## Acceptance Criteria

- `AC-243-01` — The default lifecycle keeps 7 days of raw event, state and provenance detail, at most 30 days of anomaly detail, 30 days of hourly summaries, and 365 days of daily summaries, with deterministic snapshot downsampling.
- `AC-243-02` — Current in-scope state remains available independently of historical-detail retention, tombstones remain only as long as required by the declared history window, and compaction cannot recreate a deleted object or erase an active object.
- `AC-243-03` — Retention runs at startup, at least every six hours while active, and near the 512 MiB default ceiling; pressure first compacts eligible detail, then evicts globally oldest history while persisting a RetentionRun and CoverageGap for forced loss.
- `AC-243-04` — MCP inline export temporaries are destroyed after each response; manual exports remain user-owned and are never automatically deleted, while ExportRecords report bounded inventory, hash, time range, precision, path-detail policy, and creation status.
- `AC-243-05` — Lifecycle status reports requested versus actually retained intervals, oldest and newest timestamps and counts per tier, database bytes versus cap, last compaction, forced evictions, current-state size, export inventory, and known gaps.

## Required Evidence

- `EVREQ-243-01` (lifecycle-and-pressure-test) — Boundary fixtures for every tier and snapshot rule, current-state survival, tombstone expiry, near-cap and over-cap behavior, persisted loss diagnostics, restart scheduling, and manual versus temporary exports.
